findings.claim: Mark schemes reward candidates who identify non-financial rewards too
findings.truth: No published OCR mark scheme is quoted or knowable here. The advice is sound; the attribution to a mark scheme is invented.
findings.evidence: house rule on fabricated examiner claims

findings.claim: he co-founded BrewDog in Aberdeen
findings.truth: BrewDog was founded in Fraserburgh, Aberdeenshire, in 2007; brewing moved to Ellon in 2012.

findings.claim: Gymshark's founding garage is given three different locations across the unit: 'his parents' Solihull garage' (L1), 'a Birmingham garage' (L7), 'a Solihull garage' (L9) and 'Gymshark, a Birmingham-founded fitness clothing brand' (L9 practice question 5).
findings.truth: Ben Francis started Gymshark in his parents' garage in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, in 2012. Solihull (Blythe Valley Park) is the later head office. The 1bn-pound valuation came with General Atlantic's investment in August 2020, not 2024.

findings.claim: Nine lessons set a '12 marks - Evaluate / Recommend' practice question (L2, L3, L5, L6, L9, L10, L11, L13, L15) and five exam tips coach 12-mark technique (L2, L4, L6, L10, L13).
findings.truth: OCR J204 tariffs run 1-9: 1-mark multiple choice in section A, then 2/3/4/6/7/9-mark questions in section B. There is no 12-mark question. Each affected question is retariffed to 9 marks and its band ladder rescaled.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/business-J204.md section 3a (80 marks per component, section A 15 marks, section B 65 marks); brief exam anchors

findings.claim: A partnership has between 2 and 20 owners
findings.truth: The 20-member cap on partnerships was repealed on 21 December 2002 by SI 2002/3203, which struck out sections 716 and 717 of the Companies Act 1985. Large UK partnerships have hundreds of partners. Changed to 'two or more'.
findings.evidence: legislation.gov.uk, Regulatory Reform (Removal of 20 Member Limit in Partnerships etc.) Order 2002

findings.claim: 'What is the maximum number of partners in a traditional partnership?' marks '20' correct and 'Unlimited' wrong.
findings.truth: The true answer is 'Unlimited'. Stem retimed to the 2002 law change and correct index moved from 2 to 3.

findings.claim: when Boohoo was linked to underpaid factory workers in Leicester, sales fell and the share price halved within days (repeated in the practice question 4 mark scheme)
findings.truth: The share price fell 46% in July 2020, but Boohoo's sales ROSE - revenue grew through 2020-21 on pandemic demand. The claim that sales fell is invented.

findings.claim: Greggs has grown ... one lease and one shop team at a time. No mergers, no takeovers.
findings.truth: Greggs did acquire businesses, notably Bakers Oven in 1994 and several regional bakery chains earlier. The organic-growth illustration survives without the categorical claim.

findings.claim: Morrisons' takeover of Safeway in 2005 instantly doubled its store count (and the flashcard 'Morrisons' 2005 takeover of Safeway')
findings.truth: The Safeway takeover completed in March 2004, not 2005. It added 479 Safeway stores to roughly 125 Morrisons stores - far more than doubling.

findings.claim: Seven invented examiner or mark-scheme claims: 'unsupported conclusions score nothing' (L6); 'examiners look for candidates who...' (L7); 'examiners credit method marks even if the final number is wrong' (L8); 'OCR mark schemes specifically state there are no marks for an unsupported judgement' (L11); 'generic answers cap around 4 marks' and 'No marks for unsupported judgements' (L12); 'OCR examiners have flagged this as the single most common wrong answer' (L15 content) and 'OCR examiner reports flag this as the most common mistake' (L15 exam tip).
findings.truth: None of these can be sourced to a published OCR mark scheme or examiner report. Each is reworded to keep the technique advice and drop the false attribution.
findings.evidence: house rule on fabricated examiner claims and copyright distancing

findings.claim: when Topshop stopped appealing to its core 16-25 segment, it collapsed into administration in 2021 (and the matching flashcard question)
findings.truth: Arcadia Group, Topshop's parent, entered administration on 30 November 2020. ASOS bought the Topshop brand out of administration in February 2021.

findings.claim: Apple has the iPhone in maturity ... and older iPod models in decline
findings.truth: Apple discontinued the last iPod (iPod touch, 7th generation) on 10 May 2022, ending the line. It is not a current portfolio product.

findings.claim: Spotify delivers music as a direct download
findings.truth: Spotify is a streaming service. Offline saving is a premium convenience, not the delivery model.

findings.claim: Tesco has supermarkets AND groceries.com
findings.truth: groceries.com is not a Tesco site. Tesco's online grocery service runs at tesco.com.

findings.claim: Alongside point-of-sale and advertising, OCR names price reductions, loss leaders, competitions and free samples.
findings.truth: The spec lists price reductions, loss leaders, competitions and free samples as the points to include UNDER 'Promotion - point of sale', not as a category alongside it.

findings.claim: Approximately 10% of the paper is made up of quantitative skills
findings.truth: The spec sets a MINIMUM of 10% of overall marks across the qualification, not approximately 10% of one paper.

findings.claim: This lesson covers two OCR topics: organisational structures (tall, flat, matrix) ... Tall, flat and matrix are the three main structures.
findings.truth: Spec 3.2 names only tall and flat structures. Matrix is not examinable content for this board; it is kept but reframed as a third type worth knowing rather than a spec item.

findings.claim: OCR names full-time, part-time, temporary, zero-hour, flexible, working from home / remote, and self-employed as the main ways of working (repeated in the conclusion and the intro).
findings.truth: Spec 3.2 names full-time, part-time, flexible working, temporary work, working from home, working whilst mobile and self-employed. Zero-hour is not on that list and 'working whilst mobile' was missing from the lesson entirely. The mobile bullet now carries both.

findings.claim: OCR names specific methods: job rotation, job enrichment, team-working, award schemes, working environment, praise.
findings.truth: Spec 3.5 names praise, award schemes and working environment as the non-financial methods. Job rotation, job enrichment and team-working belong to other boards' lists; they are kept as case-study extras.

findings.claim: OCR names four key areas of employment law: minimum wage, the right to a contract, holidays and hours of work, and protection from discrimination.
findings.truth: Spec 3.7 names discrimination, employees' right to a contract, holidays and hours of work. Minimum wage is not one of the named points. It is kept as useful background, correctly labelled.

findings.claim: National Minimum Wage / National Living Wage: 'The minimum hourly rate a worker aged 21 or over must legally be paid in the UK.'
findings.truth: That describes only the National Living Wage. The National Minimum Wage covers workers under 21 and apprentices at lower rates. Definition corrected in content_html and glossary_terms.

findings.claim: Tesco spends over 300 million pounds a year on marketing (also flashcard 14: 'Give a UK company that spends over 300 million pounds a year on marketing.' -> 'Tesco.')
findings.truth: I cannot source this figure. Tesco does not publish a marketing-cost line, and independent UK advertising-spend estimates for Tesco sit nearer 70-110 million pounds a year. Options: (a) drop the number - 'Tesco spends tens of millions of pounds a year on advertising' - and reword the flashcard to 'Which UK supermarket is one of the country's biggest advertisers?'; (b) leave it and accept an unsourced statistic. My recommendation is (a): the point of the passage is scale contrast with a small bakery, which survives without a precise figure.
findings.evidence: no verifiable source found; WebSearch budget exhausted
findings.ruling: Unsourced £300m figure dropped in content and flashcard; Tesco kept as a big-advertiser example.

findings.claim: In L11, L12, L13, L14 and L15 the 1-, 2- and 3-mark practice questions carry four-band 'Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging' ladders, e.g. a 1-mark multiple choice graded 'Mastering: Correct letter (B) clearly indicated. Secure: Correct letter selected. Developing: Incorrect letter.'
findings.truth: A 1-mark multiple choice is right or wrong; a band ladder cannot apply to it, and 'Secure' vs 'Mastering' on a single letter is meaningless. Options: (a) replace the ladder on every 1-3 mark item with a plain answer plus mark allocation, matching the house style used in L1-L10; (b) leave it. My recommendation is (a), but it is a question-type relabel across roughly 20 items rather than a fact fix, so it belongs with the wider band-ladder queue, not this pass.
findings.evidence: internal consistency; L1-L10 already use plain mark allocations at these tariffs
findings.ruling: NOTE: band ladders on 1-3 mark items in L11-L15 left for the programme-wide band-ladder sweep.

findings.claim: No lesson in the unit covers spec 3.3, Communication in business.
findings.truth: Spec 3.3 requires ways of communicating (letter, email, text, phone, meeting/presentation, social media, website), the importance of business communications, and the influence of digital communication on business activity. The unit touches 'lines of communication' in L14 only. This is a coverage gap for a future build, not a fact error.

findings.claim: When Aston Martin floated as a Plc in 2018, the founders accepted public scrutiny of every quarterly result
findings.truth: Aston Martin Lagonda floated in October 2018 under Investindustrial and Kuwaiti investor ownership. Its founders date from 1913 and had no part in the decision. 'Its owners' would be accurate.

findings.claim: Premier League football, I'm a Celebrity and the X Factor are used by big UK advertisers (and a knowledge-check option 'A TV advert during X Factor')
findings.truth: The X Factor last aired in 2018 and was formally ended in 2021, so it is not a current advertising vehicle. Harmless as an example, but stale.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, The X Factor (British TV series)

findings.claim: Tesco Bank is a real UK example - it gave Tesco a way to earn money outside groceries
findings.truth: Tesco sold Tesco Bank's retail banking business to Barclays in 2024. The diversification point holds historically; present tense is now stale.

findings.claim: John Lewis pays a partnership bonus based on annual profit
findings.truth: John Lewis Partnership has paid no partnership bonus since 2022. Profit sharing remains a valid concept, but the present-tense example is stale.

findings.claim: Between 2010 and the early 2020s Aldi and Lidl climbed from under 5% to roughly 18% combined
findings.truth: Roughly 18% combined is a 2024-25 level (Aldi about 10%, Lidl about 8%). In the early 2020s the combined share was nearer 15%. The direction and the teaching point are right; the end date is a few years early.

findings.claim: Four lesson descriptions already exceed the 100-character validator limit: L1 (106), L3 (106), L4 (111), L5 (111).
findings.truth: Pre-existing, not introduced by this pass, and outside the fact-check remit - but it may block the apply step if the validator checks the whole row. Suggested trims if needed: L1 'What enterprise is, what makes an entrepreneur, and the risk-reward trade-off of starting up.' (93); L3 'Sole traders, partnerships, Ltds and Plcs - features and what limited liability really means.' (94); L4 'Profit, survival, growth, service and market share - why objectives differ and change.' (86); L5 'Who has a stake in a business, how business activity affects them, and how they affect it.' (90).

summary: 15 lessons checked, 30 findings, 64 edits. The dominant defect is a fabricated 12-mark tariff: nine lessons set a 12-mark Evaluate/Recommend question and five exam tips coach 12-mark technique, when OCR J204 tops out at 9 marks. Beyond that: three wrong case-study years or outcomes (Morrisons/Safeway 2005, Topshop 2021, Boohoo 'sales fell'), a Gymshark founding location given three different ways, seven invented examiner or mark-scheme claims, and four places where a list is attributed to OCR that does not match the spec (matrix structures, ways of working, non-financial motivation, employment law). All calculations and answer keys were recomputed and every one is correct.
